Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this on — ACME's security team is getting our Q3 audit calendar in order and we'd like to confirm a few things before we proceed with the formal evidence request. We're planning a combined ISO 27001 gap assessment and FedRAMP readiness check in late September, and want to scope Redwood's intake so we can lock a window with our audit partner.

High-level questions: 
- Can you confirm whether production backups are retained in a customer-segmented store (we need retention windows and controls)?
- Do you have a current network diagram that shows peering/VPC boundaries for the hosted service and Dedicated?
- Which of the following artifacts can you provide within a 10 business-day window after we issue the request: SOC 2 Type 1/2 report (if available), encryption key lifecycle policy, evidence of vulnerability management scans?

Lastly, our auditors will want to schedule a 60-minute scoping call next week (preferred window Tue/Wed). Can you let me know who on your side will own evidence intake and whether you'll be able to supply the initial bundle as attachments or via a secure drive link?

Appreciate it — cc'ing procurement for timing considerations.

Best,

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and a proposed plan below.

Short answers: 
- Production backups: Yes — production backups are stored in a tenant-scoped object store. Retention policy defaults to 90 days; retention extension is available via contract. We'll include the retention policy document.
- Network diagram: I can attach the latest simplified network diagram (production VPCs, peering, Dedicated overlay).
- Fast-turn artifacts: we can typically provide the following within 10 business days: encryption key lifecycle policy, vulnerability scan summaries (last 90 days), and the network diagram. SOC 2 reports are on a scheduled cadence — we can provide the latest readiness summary and expected date for Type 2 delivery.

Proposed intake flow: 
1) Scoping call — 45 mins: go over audit timeline, confirm controls in scope (ISO clauses + FedRAMP baselines), and agree on evidence owners.
2) Redwood will publish an evidence bundle to a secure GDrive folder and send individual signed links for sensitive items (KMS attestations).
3) If ThirdEye needs a deeper walkthrough (architectural Q&A), we'll follow with a technical deep-dive.

Availability for scoping call: Tue 18 Aug 09:30-11:30 PT or Wed 19 Aug 14:00-16:00 PT. Who should be on the call from your side?

I'll attach: Network-Diagram.png and a one-page evidence intake checklist to set expectations. Mina will own evidence collection; Marcus will be looped for any escalation or SLA exceptions.

Thanks,

—
Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
